overview: This file traces changes in the governorship and senior administration of Japanese colonial Taiwan between 1931 and 1937. Its telegrams and consular despatches cover the resignations following the Musha Incident, the appointments of Masahiro Ōta, Kenzo Nakagawa, and Seizō Kobayashi, the resulting turnover among subordinate officials, and concern that political patronage was weakening administrative continuity. The reports also describe reactions among business associations, provincial notables, military authorities, Japanese residents, and prominent Taiwanese Chinese; assess possible consequences for the Sun Moon Lake hydroelectric project; and report Kobayashi’s proposed goodwill tour of Southeast Asian colonies and ports.

subfiles.title: Telegram from Reed on the governor-general’s resignation
subfiles.about: Reports the anticipated resignation of senior Taiwan officials after the Musha Incident and assesses the likely effect on the Sun Moon Lake project.
subfiles.summary: Reed reports the Governor-General resigned over the Musha Incident, predicting other department heads might follow, unlikely to affect the Candidius hydroelectric project.

subfiles.title: Despatch on resignations and new Taiwan officials
subfiles.from: Charles S. Reed II, American Vice Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.about: Explains the resignations following the Musha Incident, identifies the incoming leadership, and considers political and commercial consequences.
subfiles.summary: Reed reports Governor-General Ishizuka's and others' resignations, Ōta's appointment as successor and Takahashi as Director General, noting Takahashi's unusual consular outreach; he sees the changes as reducing Diet criticism of the Hamaguchi government over the Musha uprising.

subfiles.title: Department memorandum summarizing Despatch No. 24
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Taihoku despatch on the new governor-general and dissatisfaction with frequent gubernatorial changes.
subfiles.summary: Memo summarizes Despatch No. 24 on a new Governor-General's appointment, noting dissatisfaction over five governors in three years and support for a military appointee.

subfiles.title: Despatch on the appointment of Kenzo Nakagawa
subfiles.from: John B. Ketcham, American Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.about: Reports Kenzo Nakagawa’s appointment and protests against politically driven turnover in Taiwan’s colonial administration.
subfiles.summary: Ketcham reports Kenzo Nakagawa's appointment as Governor-General after Minami resigned following Premier Inukai's assassination, detailing Nakagawa's biography and mounting Taiwanese and business protests against the spoils system, amid sympathy for a military governor-general.

subfiles.title: Cross-reference to Neville despatch on Kobayashi’s appointment
subfiles.about: Directs readers to another decimal-file item concerning Nakagawa’s resignation and Kobayashi’s appointment.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Neville's 1936 despatch on Nakagawa's resignation and Admiral Kobayashi's appointment as Governor-General of Formosa.

subfiles.title: Despatch on Kobayashi’s proposed South Seas tour
subfiles.from: Alvin T. Rowe Jr., American Vice Consul, Taihoku
subfiles.about: Reports Governor-General Kobayashi’s contemplated goodwill tour of Southeast Asia and nearby colonial territories.
subfiles.summary: Rowe reports press speculation that Admiral Kobayashi planned a South Seas tour (Philippines, Netherlands East Indies, Siam, Indochina, Hong Kong) after Japan's April election, possibly aboard a naval vessel with Taiwan business leaders.

interest: Shows repeated political turnover reshaping colonial Taiwan's administration, tied to protest, infrastructure finance, and regional diplomacy.
